name: @tellma/core-ui
description: Tellma UI component library — tm-* form controls built on @angular/cdk + @angular/aria, signal-first, Signal Forms native.

Set to 8.71, the measured 8.61 plus 0.1 KB, once the grid's list-page work merged with the work that landed meanwhile. Earlier raised from 8.5 to 9 for the grid's list-page strings (the row-activation hint, the sort and sort-cleared announcements, the across-pages checked count, the new-tab key label and the reworded Enter and F2 key labels): measured 8.48 before and 8.61 after (+0.13 KB); the strings are the payload, so there is nothing to fold. Re-measured after TmClientCache.clearAll grew from one CacheStorage sweep into the four-area sweep with its keep predicate (IndexedDB databases enumerated and deleted without waiting on blocked deletes, localStorage and sessionStorage keys): 8.12 before, 8.42 after (+0.30 KB); 8.48 once merged with the work that landed meanwhile, under the unchanged 8.5. Raised from 8 to 8.5 for the grid's keyboard help labels (30 English strings under grid.keys, one per help row of the grid's published key list): measured 7.82 before and 8.12 after (+0.30 KB); the strings are the payload, so there is nothing to fold. Previously raised from 5 to 8. About 1.1 KB is the foundation seams the app shell builds on: TmBreakpoints over five media query lists, TmTheme with its System tracking, the live root Directionality, the translations loader and the touch-size resolver. About 1.4 KB is the ICU MessageFormat interpreter that replaced the eval-based compiler, so messages format under a script-src 'self' Content Security Policy with no 'unsafe-eval'; the old compiler lived in an external @jsverse package outside this measurement, so the app bundle itself shrinks (it no longer carries @messageformat/core and its plural data). The instant and time-zone additions that headroom was kept for have landed: the display-zone, device-zone and clock tokens and the formatting facade's instant, zone-label, relative-time and name members took the measured weight from 7.18 to 7.79, leaving about 0.2 KB.
budgetNotes../l10n: Raised from 8 to 10 for instants and period formatting: measured 7.65 before and 9.50 after (+1.85 KB). The weight is the instant parser, the date-time, time and relative-time formatters with their zone arithmetic (offsets, calendar days in a zone, daylight-saving days), the zone offset and zone name labels and the label decision, the month, quarter, year and weekday date styles, month and weekday names, the grouping option, and the stripping of bidirectional control characters from every formatter's output. Kept down by one cached Intl formatter factory shared by every instant path and by the instant formats reusing the date engine's style table.
budgetNotes../popover: Raised from 4 to 4.5 for keeping open popovers inside the viewport: the width cap is written from the visible viewport width (100vw counted a classic scrollbar, so a clamped panel ran under it), and the height cap, width cap and inline offset are re-fitted on every scroll and resize while open (the CDK reports a placement only when its side changes). Measured 4087 B before these fixes and 4228 B after (+141 B net); the saving taken in the same change was folding the three fixed-size width rules into one custom property read by the base rule. The entry point holds the fixed sizes, the viewport fitting and the block cap.
budgetNotes../entity-picker: Raised from 11 to 12 for the in-field invalid glyph the picker now draws itself (the field can only append its own AFTER the whole control, which would shove the magnifier sideways every time an error came and went). Previously raised from 10 to 11. The picker measures ~10.5 KB as one eager surface: it is an editable combobox that also carries an async search lifecycle, a text/value resolution channel, three modal pages, and a grid cell-editor implementation. The remaining lever is deferring the popup into its own chunk (the date-picker's shape), which is a change to the mounting sequence this control's overlay placement and highlight protocol are sensitive to — not worth reopening for 0.5 KB. Revisit if the popup is extracted for other reasons.
budgetNotes../alert: Raised from 2 to 2.25 (the measured size plus about 0.1 KB) for the four tone glyphs moving onto tm-icon: measured 1.98 before and 2.14 after (+0.16 KB). The Lucide data of info, circle-check-big, triangle-alert and circle-x weighs 0.33 KB in place; the inline SVG markup it replaces gives back about 0.17 (the template ships twice, once as metadata). The saving taken was one glyph table keyed by kind in place of four template branches; nothing else in the entry point moved. The component itself is 1.8 KB, so the glyph data is now its largest single part.
budgetNotes../image: Raised from 10 to 11 for blob cancellation and the glyphs moving onto tm-icon: measured 9.95 before and 10.69 after (+0.74 KB). The Lucide data of image-off, image, camera, crop, trash-2 and check weighs 0.64 KB in place; the rest is the cancellation (the default fetcher's abort path, the reference-counted request and revalidation sharing in the blob cache, and tm-image's per-load abort lifecycle with its viewport tracking, about 0.4 KB), less the inline SVG markup the glyphs replace (about 0.3; the template ships twice, once as metadata). Savings taken: the blob cache's request and revalidation share one reference-counting helper instead of two copies, and the per-caller wait is one promise chain. The glyph data alone exceeds the 0.05 KB of headroom this entry point had left, so no saving short of dropping a spec'd glyph or the cancellation keeps it under 10.
budgetNotes../form-field: Re-measured after the invalid mark moved onto tm-icon: 4.71 before, 4.82 after, under the unchanged 5 (the closest of the three glyph entry points to its ceiling). Previously raised from 4 to 5 for the validation popover: the field now anchors an overlay (the shared @tellma/core-ui/overlay helper plus a CdkConnectedOverlay in its template) instead of writing a message into a row. The weight is the overlay wiring, not the bubble — the bubble itself is one presentational component shared with the grid.
budgetNotes../select: Raised from 8 to 9 for tm-multi-select and option groups: measured 6.07 before and 8.28 after. The multi-select adds its own template, the joined-label trigger and its option-order commit (about 1.4); option groups add the grouped panel markup in both templates and tm-option-group itself (about 0.5); the glyphs now draw through tm-icon with Lucide data, whose component lives in ./icon and is measured there. The saving taken was moving everything both selects share (the form-control plumbing, the value bridge, closed-trigger typeahead, the panel wiring) into one base class instead of a second copy, and sharing one stylesheet for the select chrome.
budgetNotes../checkbox: Re-measured after its check and dash moved onto tm-icon: 3.06 before, 3.24 after, under the unchanged 4. The growth is the tm-icon import's component metadata and the two Lucide paths; the inline SVG it replaces was smaller as markup but drew a second, separately maintained copy of the glyph rules.
budgetNotes../icon: Raised from 2 to 3 at birth: measured 2.7. The spec's 2 was an estimate below the real logic: the registry and the icon-data guard (the allowed elements, the refused event-handler and link attributes, attribute-name and kebab-case name checks, and refusal messages that are the only diagnostic a developer gets), plus the draw path (the template cache, the clone, the unknown-name and refusal reporting). The component's duplicated decorator metadata costs about 0.1 of it. Nothing here grows with the number of icons: icon data is its importer's weight.
budgetNotes../kbd: Raised from 1 to 2.5 at birth: measured 2.4. The spec's 1 was an estimate below the real logic: about 1.6 is the key-combination parser (with its two grammar errors), the matcher (the US punctuation table, the three event.code fallbacks, the AltGr rule) and the three label writers, and about 0.75 is tm-kbd itself, of which the duplicated decorator metadata is about 0.1.
budgetNotes../menu: Raised from 6 to 8.5 for the rich entry kinds: measured 8.4, up from 4.4. The planned ceiling was 7; that estimate sat below the real surface. Of the 4.0 added, about 1.9 is the row renderer (three row shapes: link, submenu parent, item; groups; the icon forms, second line, detail, key caps and glyphs; the link and keep-open activation rules; the development diagnostics), about 0.4 the submenu overlay, about 0.4 the menu-button trigger, about 0.3 the stylesheet, about 0.2 the dismissal and key-timing rules (the release of the right-click that opened the menu, held keys, keys pressed between an open and its render), and the rest the header block, focus on open and the trigger registration in tm-menu itself. Templates ship as source text in the measured build, so the three row shapes cost their markup, not compiled code. The three Lucide glyphs (check, chevron, external link) are 0.2 KB raw. Savings taken: a trimming pass took the first measurement down by 0.14 (8.35 to 8.21, before the 0.2 of dismissal and key-timing rules): the new-tab note moved into the row's accessible name, which dropped a visually hidden element and its style rule; the description ids are minted once per row instead of in the markup; one helper types the shared row template's context in place of repeated casts; the group rule left the stylesheet; the development messages were shortened. The submenu's own Escape registration was then folded into the menu's. Options measured and not taken, none of which reaches 7: leaving the three glyphs outside the entry point gives 8.14; stripping the development diagnostics gives 8.27; moving the trigger to an entry point of its own saves about 0.4. Each drops or relocates something this entry point is specified to hold.
budgetNotes../grid: Raised from 39 to 42 for the list-page features (row activation and its 400 ms guard, the two-way active row with the search-field driver directive, the two-way sort with its header slot, select-all across pages, row classes, optional row headers and the scrollbar gutter): measured 38.73 before and 41.92 after (+3.19 KB), the ceiling set for the grid's list features before popup editors. Review fixes (a pen long-press, a held Enter and a right-click on a cell link no longer open or move what they should not) took it to 42.00, held at the ceiling by dropping the header sort view model's flag (a header that does not sort holds no entry). About 0.8 KB is template and stylesheet text, which ships twice in the decorator metadata; the rest is the activation, sort and active-row logic in the core, the driver and the new inputs and models. Savings taken (-0.10 KB): one cell test shared by the press, middle-click and tap paths in place of three lookups, shorter development errors and template comments. This is the third raise of this ceiling; the spec that sets 42 leaves no room for its header navigation, scrollToRow, tree expansion and row-end column, so the entry point needs the re-split this note called for. Previously raised from 38.5 to 39 for the key map through kbd and the glyphs through tm-icon: measured 38.04 before and 38.71 after (+0.68 KB). The weight is the one binding table (every key combination with its intent and help label, which the published key list is derived from), the matching loop over its letter and symbol bindings, and the Lucide data of the thirteen glyphs the find bar, status bar, tree expander and context menu now draw through tm-icon; the deleted icon-template component and the two platform sniffs give back part of it. Savings looked for and not found: the 30 label keys share a prefix that gzip already folds; drawing the glyphs through another entry point would only move their bytes, since each entry point is measured on its own weight; and the table cannot shed its intents or conditions, which the resolver runs on. This is the second raise of this ceiling under the raise-by-what-it-adds rule; a third re-splits the entry point instead. Previously raised from 38 to 38.5 for the left-to-right run around a number cell's text (formatted numbers no longer carry direction marks, so markup keeps a minus at the left of its digits in a right-to-left grid): measured 38909 B before and about 38995 B after (+85 B: one attribute binding and one view-model field, against 3 B of headroom); the touched lines held nothing to fold. Previously raised from 37 to 38 for the shared validation bubble (the cell error now renders the same component the form field does, so a cell error and a field error cannot drift apart). Previously raised from 36 to 37 for the typed-commit search rung (the editor's own search decides a commit before the column's label resolver is asked). NOTE the standing gap: spec 0004 set grid at 24 KB and the measured surface has never been near it — this ceiling has climbed 34 -> 35 -> 36 -> 37 -> 38 -> 38.5 -> 39 across four specs, each time as a ratchet over measured reality. Worth a dedicated pass rather than another increment.
budgetNotes../avatar: Raised from 2 to 2.75 at birth: measured 2.63, unchanged in review, with about 0.1 of headroom. The spec's 2 was an estimate below the real surface: tmInitials (grapheme segmentation with a per-locale segmenter cache, the cased-script test and the locale's upper-casing), the FNV-1a tone hash, the component with its photo-or-face template and the person glyph's Lucide data, and a stylesheet with five sizes and eight keyed tones. The saving review found elsewhere was already in place here: the tone rides one data-tone attribute matched by attribute selectors, not a class per tone. The duplicated decorator metadata (template and styles a second time) is about 0.23 of it (9%) once gzip folds it: the build's output, not a lever.
budgetNotes../badge: Raised from 1 to 2.2 at birth: measured 2.08 (2.17 before review), with about 0.1 of headroom. The entry point holds two components, tm-badge (six tones, the dot and the icon, the label's ellipsis) and tm-counter (the cap through the translated overflow string, locale digits in an isolated left-to-right run, three tones, the overlay placement with its halo, the reserved two-digit width and the forced-colours rule); the spec's 1 budgeted for one. Saving taken: one data-tone attribute binding matched by attribute selectors, in place of six tone-class bindings on tm-badge and two on tm-counter (-0.09). The duplicated decorator metadata (template and styles a second time) is about 0.3 of it (14%) once gzip folds it: the build's output, not a lever.
budgetNotes../copy: Raised from 1 to 3.3 at birth: measured 3.20 (3.16 before review), with about 0.1 of headroom. The +0.04 is the guards that stop a copy settling after the button is destroyed from emitting, arming timers or opening the fallback. The entry point holds two components: tm-copy-button (the in-click write, the pending-item write for a value built on the click, the manual fallback with its selected read-only input, its own tooltip and its place on the Escape stack, the live region, the reserved labelled width, the copy and check glyphs) and tm-reference; the spec's 1 budgeted for a bare button. Option measured and not taken: one button element for both forms, with the icon-only tooltip run by hand instead of a tmTooltip in a second template, measured 3.25. That is heavier than the two-template form, because the hand-run tooltip costs more than the markup it saves. The duplicated decorator metadata (template and styles a second time) is about 0.28 of it (9%) once gzip folds it: the build's output, not a lever.
budgetNotes../empty-state: Raised from 1 to 1.4 at birth: measured 1.30 (1.32 before review), with about 0.1 of headroom. The template is the icon, heading, detail and actions slots, and the live region filled a microtask after insertion. The stylesheet holds the page and panel sizes, the error tone and the collapsed empty slots. Saving taken: data-size and data-tone attribute bindings in place of three class bindings (-0.02). The duplicated decorator metadata (template and styles a second time) is about 0.19 of it (14%) once gzip folds it: the build's output, not a lever.
budgetNotes../progress: Raised from 1 to 2.7 at birth: measured 2.56 (2.60 before review), with about 0.1 of headroom. The entry point holds two components: tm-progress-bar (the minimum-display hold timed by the injected clock and read from its token, the clamped value, four tones, the sweep in both directions, the reduced-motion and forced-colours rules) and tm-progress-ring (the SVG ring, the spin, the named non-decorative mode with its development warning); the spec's 1 budgeted for one. Saving taken: one data-tone attribute binding matched by attribute selectors, in place of three tone-class bindings on the bar (-0.04, net of the per-tone fill tokens added in the same change). Not taken: shortening the ring's one-sentence development warning, which follows the library's isDevMode() convention and is the only diagnostic a developer gets. The duplicated decorator metadata (template and styles a second time) is about 0.36 of it (14%) once gzip folds it: the build's output, not a lever.
budgetNotes../relative-time: Raised from 1 to 1.35 at birth: measured 1.21, unchanged in review, with about 0.1 of headroom. The component is small; the rest is the shared minute ticker (minute-boundary scheduling, the reader count, and the visibility listener that stops it and catches it up). There is no per-variant binding to fold. The duplicated decorator metadata (template and styles a second time) is about 0.14 of it (12%) once gzip folds it: the build's output, not a lever.
budgetNotes../skeleton: Raised from 1 to 1.65 at birth: measured 1.53 (1.58 before review), with about 0.1 of headroom. Four shapes share one template (line bars, block, circle, and the table's header and body rows of cells). The stylesheet sizes the table rows from the grid's row heights for the workspace size step. Saving taken: one data-shape attribute binding in place of four shape-class bindings (-0.05). The duplicated decorator metadata (template and styles a second time) is about 0.22 of it (14%) once gzip folds it: the build's output, not a lever.
budgetNotes._: Ceilings are ratchets. Any raise belongs here with its reason; a raise with no note is a bug.
